description: Shared Rust <-> WASM vectors for action_from_command risk on command lines with shell operators, substitutions, redirections and newlines (issue #272). Expected values are derived by hand from the risk table and rule in crates/allw-core/src/command.rs (shell_line_risk) and docs/policy-seam.md; bin is always the first shlex word (unchanged by #272). Append-only.

cases.why: && runs rm -rf /: High
|| runs rm -rf /: High
& backgrounds ls, then runs rm -rf /: High
; runs rm -rf / (bin keeps the shlex word ls;)
a newline separates two commands
a pipe is shell syntax: at least Medium; sh alone is Medium
command substitution runs rm -rf ~
backtick substitution runs rm -rf ~
double quotes do not stop command substitution
process substitution runs rm -rf ~
nested substitution is analyzed
a redirection is shell syntax: at least Medium
a redirection is shell syntax; 2>&1 is not a command
the second command is a force push
the second command is dd: Critical
the then-branch runs rm -rf /; keywords are skipped

cases.command: for f in a; do rm -rf $f; done
cases.why: the loop body runs rm -rf; keywords are skipped
a brace group runs rm -rf /
a subshell runs rm -rf /
eval runs its arguments as a command line
eval runs its arguments as a command line
the quote is inside a comment; the next line still runs
in bash $'\'' is one quote character, so the next line runs
a comment is also read as code; the higher reading wins
arithmetic expansion is read like a substitution: at least Medium
single-quoted operators are literal
double-quoted operators are literal
backslash-escaped operators are literal
single quotes stop substitution
a quoted newline is literal
a variable reference is not a substitution
a plain command is unchanged
a plain command is unchanged
